handback.t:
CAP-2 (f2 efficiency & memory) is done. All three parts are built and measured, and the VERIFY REQUEST block is appended to `results/research_board.md` with exact rerun commands (`CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/Users/mariu/nm-target-hr`). `src/` is untouched, there are no new crates, nothing was downloaded, and no git commits were made. I used only `nm-target-r3`.

**Protocol**
- Tuning used seeds 1-8, held-out was 31-60, and confirm was 61-90 frozen.
- I added a 91-250 "power extension" (160 fresh seeds, frozen, never used for any choice), because 30 seeds cannot resolve the 0.003 margin in the noisy worlds. This is a disclosed deviation from your protocol.
- Quality is paired 95% t-CI against the full-precision / always-full baseline, with TOST equivalence at margin 0.003 and Holm across cells.
- I claim "lossless" only if Holm p < 0.05 and the CI sits inside ±0.003.
- Worlds: sim Fixed, Random and NoTraps, plus my own 32-agent world (my construction).
- Self-tests at start of `f2_quant`: my compact router (f64) makes the same decisions as `HebbianRouter` inside `Warm`, and the packed state round-trips exactly.

**(a) Memory (`f2_quant`)**
- **Lossless in all 4 worlds:** block-float 16-bit rows with stochastic rounding, f32 and (trivially) the f64 reference. Block-float 16 gives dQ within ±0.0010 on 160 seeds and 99.98% same-history decision agreement. This is 10.4 KB against 25.5 KB for packed f64 in the 32-agent world, and 915 B against 2.1 KB in the sims.
- **Lossless in the 3 sim worlds only:** f16 and x3's u16 (fixed point). Neither is CI-bounded in the 32-agent world.
- **Bytes caveat:** most of the 15x (32-agent world) / 5.8x (sim) saving against the JSON state the CLI persists today comes from binary encoding and sparse rows, not quantisation. Quantisation itself adds 2.4x (16-bit) to 3.2x (8-bit) on top.
- **8-bit block-float (7.9 KB):** sim loss is ≤0.001, but it is not CI-bounded, and the 32-agent world shows -0.0038 [-0.0085, +0.0008].
- **x3's u8 failure reproduces** at -0.05 to -0.07. Stochastic rounding recovers most of it but still loses 0.008-0.014. 4-bit loses 0.015-0.033.
- **Per-row adaptive precision did not help.** Tuning found no rule that qualified.
- **Pruning cold rows loses quality.** In the 32-agent world, 50% of rows (5.4 KB) gives -0.0053 [-0.0110, +0.0005]. Sims lose far more, because every row is useful there.

**(b) Parallel routing (`f2_parallel`)**
- **Decisions are bit-identical to serial** for every state, variant and thread count. The crate router and my compact router also agree on 20,000 tasks.
- **Single-thread speedup is real.** The crate's `HebbianRouter::select` clones feature strings on every call (2.8 µs/task). My version does the same job in 0.31-0.42 µs, a 6.8-9x gain (12-14x on the 128-agent state). It is an implementation speedup, not extra capacity.
- **Threads, 16 logical cores:**
  - 4 threads: about 3.8-4.0x.
  - 8 threads: about 4.2-4.8x.
  - 16 threads: about 5.7-7.2x in the cleanest run, and 3.6-8.4x across three runs.
  - The machine was shared with other jobs at 70-100% CPU, so treat this as ±25%.
- **Small batches:** spawning threads per call loses below about 2k tasks. A persistent pool breaks even at about 256 tasks and reaches 8.5x at 262k.
- **Not a compute multiplier.** The same work is done and per-task latency does not improve. Updates are 47% of the loop, which caps whole-loop speedup at about 2x (Amdahl). Routing a batch of 4 on frozen state costs about 0.001-0.003 in quality (not shown equivalent). A batch of 64 costs 0.005-0.016 and a batch of 256 costs 0.01-0.05.

**(c) Scheduler (`f2_sched`)**
- **Setup:** cheap path (keyword or a memoised best agent) when confident, else the full router. I froze 3 operating points from the 8 tuning seeds and ran a random-gate control at the same full-router fraction.
- **No operating point passes the equivalence test** in any world, so "lossless" is not claimed.
- **The strict point (A) needs about 80% full-router calls and saves nothing**; its estimated cost is slightly above always-full.
- **The looser points (B, C)** use 13-51% full-router calls, with estimated ns/task cut 36-68%.
  - **Loss:** the worst CI lower bound is -0.0042.
  - **Gains:** they are better than always-full in the no-traps and 32-agent worlds (up to +0.029).
  - **Versus a random gate at the same fraction:** they are far ahead (+0.05-0.08 in the trap sims).
  - **Versus `guarded(x1)`:** they win in the trap sims and lose in no-traps, so this is a cost-aware variant, not a better router.
- **Latency:** median drops, but p99 gets worse (about 3.0 → 5.5 µs). The mean moved from -5% to -41% across runs on the shared box.
- **Cost caveat:** both paths cost microseconds here. Any real saving assumes an expensive full path, which is an assumption, not a measurement.
